gabes.title: Gabès: The City Paying the Price of Pollution
gabes.narrative: For decades, Gabès has carried the environmental cost of Tunisia’s industrial model. In 2026, pollution, public health, industrial policy and political accountability remain inseparable.

EV-GABES-01.headline: Historical Phosphogypsum Sludge Marine Discharge Baseline
EV-GABES-01.summary: Between 1979 and 2018, Groupe Chimique Tunisien (GCT) industrial complex discharged an estimated nominal 14,000 to 15,000 tonnes per day of phosphogypsum slurry directly into the maritime waters of the Gulf of Gabès.
EV-GABES-01.claim: Historical industrial assessment of dry-solid phosphogypsum runoff into the Gulf of Gabès.
EV-GABES-01.source_name: Ministère de l'Environnement (ANPE) / World Bank Environmental Audit

EV-GABES-02.headline: 2017 Cabinet Decision on GCT Unit Dismantling and Coastal Relocation
EV-GABES-02.summary: On June 29, 2017, the Cabinet of Ministers formally announced the decision to dismantle the polluting chemical processing units of GCT in Gabès and relocate them away from residential zones to a designated inland site.
EV-GABES-02.claim: Government committed to full environmental dismantling of coastal units.
EV-GABES-02.source_name: Presidency of the Government (Cabinet Meeting Communiqué)

EV-GABES-03.headline: Current Real-Time Direct Discharge Monitoring Status
EV-GABES-03.summary: No public continuous online sensor telemetry is currently made available by the state or industrial operator to verify 2026 real-time discharge volumes or atmospheric SO2 spikes in Chatt Essalam.
EV-GABES-03.claim: Absence of real-time public telemetry data.

EV-WATER-01.headline: National Dam Reservoir Storage Capacity at 21.4%
EV-WATER-01.summary: National Observatory of Agriculture (ONAGRI) reported national dam reservoir storage volume at 495 million m³ against a total nominal design capacity of 2,320 million m³, representing 21.4% saturation.
EV-WATER-01.claim: Empirical dam reserves recorded at historic low levels.
EV-WATER-01.presidential_response: Attributed water cuts to criminal networks

EV-ENERGY-01.headline: STEG Electricity Grid Peak Demand Reaches 4,825 MW
EV-ENERGY-01.summary: STEG national dispatch telemetry recorded peak instantaneous electricity demand of 4,825 MW during extreme 46.2°C thermal waves, requiring emergency load shedding and Algerian gas supply activations.
EV-ENERGY-01.claim: Thermal wave pushed national grid beyond domestic thermal generation baseline.
EV-ENERGY-01.source_name: Société Tunisienne de l'Électricité et du Gaz (STEG)
EV-ENERGY-01.presidential_response: Convened emergency meeting with energy minister

EV-WORK-01.headline: INS Labor Force Survey: Graduate Unemployment at 38.6%
EV-WORK-01.summary: National Institute of Statistics (INS) Q2 2026 labor market indicators recorded national unemployment at 16.2%, with tertiary graduate joblessness reaching 38.6% (and over 44% for women in interior governorates).
EV-WORK-01.claim: Graduate joblessness structural disparities documented in interior regions.

EV-MIGRATION-01.headline: National Guard Documents 34,200+ Maritime Interceptions (Jan-Aug 2026)
EV-MIGRATION-01.summary: Maritime National Guard dispatches and FTDES field registers documented over 34,200 intercepted individuals at sea off Sfax, Kerkennah, and Zarzis coasts between January and August 2026.
EV-MIGRATION-01.claim: Intensified sea interception and containment operations along eastern littoral.
EV-MIGRATION-01.source_name: FTDES / Ministry of Interior Operational Registry
EV-MIGRATION-01.presidential_response: Affirmed Tunisia will not be a transit/resettlement country

EV-INSTITUTIONS-01.headline: Tunisian Bar Association Documents 70+ Decree 54 Prosecutions
EV-INSTITUTIONS-01.summary: Tunisian Order of Lawyers (ONAT) and SNJT recorded over 70 formal judicial prosecutions opened under Article 24 of Decree-Law 54 against defense lawyers, journalists, and civic commentators.
EV-INSTITUTIONS-01.claim: Legal brief filed documenting widespread application of Article 24 against public commentary.
EV-INSTITUTIONS-01.source_name: Ordre National des Avocats de Tunisie (ONAT) / SNJT
